events.text: The rite is short and very old. In the hall of the house, before both factions of {b3_house}, your name is cut into the Cloud Tablets. The Elders of the Tablets keep their faces still. The Young Branches do not bother to. Afterwards an old woman of the blood you have never met presses your hand and says, "Now you are ours to scold."

choices.text: Thank her, and mean it

effects.log: She scolds you at once, for standing badly. It is the warmest thing that has happened to you in years.

choices.text: Bow to the elders who voted against you

effects.log: Some of them bow back. One does not, and will remember that you bowed first.

choices.text: Find the youngest of the blood and learn their names

effects.log: By evening you know eleven names, and three of them have decided you are interesting.

events.text: The first year as one of {b3_house} is mostly small things: which door you may use now, which table, which cousin will never forgive the vote. You learn them one at a time, in the cloud terrace, the way you once learned a sword.

choices.text: Learn the house's old rules properly

effects.log: The rules are absurd and very old, and you learn every one. The elders notice.

choices.text: Break one small rule on purpose, and apologise

effects.log: In the cloud terrace, the Young Branches laugh about it for a month, and the Elders of the Tablets pretend not to.

events.text: The vote is counted in the hall of the house while you wait outside. When the doors open, nobody needs to tell you. One of the Young Branches stops on the way out and says, quietly, that it was close, and that close is not nothing.

choices.text: Go home and keep serving the house anyway

effects.log: They notice. Houses always notice who comes back after a no.

events.text: In a side room of the hall of the house, {npc} closes the screen behind you and sits down very carefully, as if the room might be listening. "If this goes wrong," {he} says, "I was never here. If it goes right, I was always here." {He} wants to know exactly what you mean to do with the head seat of {b3_house}.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth

effects.log: {npc} listens to all of it and says nothing for a long time. Then {he} nods once.

choices.text: Tell {him} what {he} wants to hear

effects.log: {npc} smiles. You are not sure whether that smile believed you.

events.text: You and {npc} meet where nobody of {b3_house} goes: the sea of clouds at night, with nothing between you and the dark. {He} brings a list of names in {his} head and will not write any of them down. "The house is not loyal to the head," {he} says. "It is loyal to the seat. Remember that when you sit in it."

choices.text: Ask who would stand against you

effects.log: {npc} names three, and the reasons. Two of them surprise you.

choices.text: Ask what {he} wants for this

effects.log: "A seat at the table," {npc} says. "And for you to remember who sat with you in the dark."

events.text: {b3_house} offers you a better title, a finer room, and an oath to swear before the Elders of the Tablets: that you hold no design on the head seat. The offer is very generous. From now on somebody sits near you at every meal.

choices.text: Swear it, and keep your face still

effects.log: You swear it in a clear voice. The oath hangs on you like a borrowed robe.

choices.text: Swear it, and wonder if you should keep it

effects.log: You swear it. That night you lie awake turning it over, which is more than they expected.

choices.text: Decline the title politely

effects.log: The house hears the no inside the politeness, as it was meant to.

events.text: In the hall of the house, the servant who brings your tea has never brought it before, and does not look at you. You let the cup go cold. Later you learn that the servant has left {b3_house} in the night, with no bundle and no goodbye.

choices.text: Say nothing, and change your rooms

effects.log: You change your rooms, and the time you sleep, and the way you come home.

choices.text: Let the house see that you noticed

effects.log: You leave the cold cup on the steps of the hall of the house, untouched. The message is read.

events.text: A letter is found in the wrong place, in a hand very like yours. In the hall of the house people stop talking when you come in. Somebody of {b3_house} has decided to be rid of you the slow way.

choices.text: Find the forger

effects.log: You find the forger, a frightened junior who was told what to write. You let them go.

choices.text: Answer the lie in front of everyone

effects.log: You stand in the hall and say what you did and did not write. Half of them believe you.

events.text: The head seat of {b3_house} is colder than it looked from below. The Elders of the Tablets kneel in rows and do not look up. The Young Branches look at you as if you were a storm that might turn either way. Behind the screens somebody is already writing the version of today the house will tell its children.

choices.text: Raise the old head's people up from the floor yourself

effects.log: You raise them one by one. Some of them hate you less for it.

choices.text: Let them stay kneeling a while

effects.log: They kneel until their knees ache. Nobody in the house will forget the length of it.

events.text: You come to on the far side of the cloud gate of {b3_house}, your things beside you in a neat bundle somebody took the time to tie. The gate is shut. It will not open for you again in this life, and everyone who passes on the road knows why.

choices.text: Pick up the bundle and walk

effects.log: You walk, and do not look back, which is the only thing left that is yours to decide.

effects.log: You bow to it. Somebody on the wall sees, and tells the house, and the house is not sure what to make of it.

events.text: At dinner in the hall of the house, a child of {b3_house} asks loudly why the new head sits in grandfather's chair. The table goes silent. Every grown face at it waits to see what you will do with a child's question.

choices.text: Answer the child honestly

effects.log: You tell the child, simply, how it happened. The child thinks about it and goes back to eating. The table breathes again.

choices.text: Say it is your chair now

effects.log: The child nods. The grown ones look at their bowls for the rest of the meal.

events.text: In a side room of {b3_house}, a cousin of the old head keeps the old head's lamp burning, and every year on the day you took the seat, the lamp is carried once around the cloud terrace in silence. Nobody has ever asked your permission.

choices.text: Walk behind the lamp

effects.log: You walk behind it, in silence, the whole way around. The next year there are fewer people watching, and more walking.

choices.text: Let them carry it without you

effects.log: They carry it. You watch from a window, and they know you are watching.

events.text: Under the clouds, {b3_beast} walks the bounds of your house with you after the trial, slower than usual, as though it wanted to be seen walking beside you. The servants stop their work to watch the two of you pass.

choices.text: Walk at its pace

effects.log: You walk at its pace the whole way round. It takes all afternoon.

choices.text: Speak to it as to an elder

effects.log: It listens, or seems to. At the gate it lies down, and sighs, satisfied.

events.text: The place across the gate of your isle where {b3_beast} lay is a flattened patch of ground now, and the servants walk around it without being told to. A child of the house leaves a bowl of water there every morning, in case.

choices.text: Leave the bowl where it is

effects.log: The bowl stays. Nobody of your house ever moves it.

choices.text: Go after it, one last time

effects.log: You follow its track for a day and stop where it stops. It is gone the way old things go, completely.

events.text: Somebody hated your house enough to plan for years, and chose {b3_beast} to strike at. You find the sign of them at the gate of your isle: careful work, and a message in it for you.

choices.text: Swear the beast will be brought back

effects.log: You swear it at the gate, where the house can hear.

choices.text: Read the message in the work

effects.log: The work tells you a little about who planned it, and a great deal about how long they have hated you.

events.text: Travellers on the road say your house's name now with the beast's in it, as if they were one word. A painter comes to paint {b3_beast} at the gate of your isle, and it lies very still for him, as if it knows what a portrait is for.

choices.text: Let the painter stay as long as he likes

effects.log: He stays a season. The painting goes into the hall, and the beast goes to look at it every evening.

choices.text: Ask for a copy for the children

effects.log: The children hang it low, where they can see it, and the beast approves.

events.text: The kingdom you fought for carries you through its streets on a door taken off its hinges, because nobody could find a proper litter in time. Children run alongside, shouting a name they have only just learned. Yours.

choices.text: Wave to every child

effects.log: Your arm is tired by the end. The children will tell their grandchildren they waved back.

choices.text: Ask them to put you down at the first well

effects.log: They put you down. You drink, and the crowd cheers the drinking as if it were a feat too.

events.text: The kings of three kingdoms sit together at the Games' last feast, which happens once every ten years and is the only time they are polite. Each of them makes you an offer between the courses. None of them is the same offer.

choices.text: Accept none of them, politely

effects.log: Three kings are refused in one evening. It becomes a story they all tell against each other.

choices.text: Accept the offer of the kingdom you fought for

effects.log: Its king beams. The other two stop smiling, and then, being kings, start again.

events.text: {npc} finds you after the Games with a cut over one eye and the look of someone who has decided something. "Ten years," {he} says. "Train. I will." {He} walks off before you can answer.

choices.text: Call after {him} that you will be ready

effects.log: {npc} raises a hand without turning round.

choices.text: Go and train that same evening

effects.log: You train until the stars come out. Somewhere across the valley, you suspect, so does {npc}.

events.text: In this age everything is done for the first time. The first bridge over the river is being built in your village, and the builders argue all day about how bridges are supposed to work, since nobody has ever seen one.

choices.text: Help them guess

effects.log: Your guess is wrong, but it is wrong in a useful direction. The bridge stands.

choices.text: Ask the oldest person in the village what the first days were like

effects.log: She was born in the second generation of the world, and remembers her mother's stories of the first dawn.

events.text: The kings hold their courts in this age, and the courts hold everything else: the roads, the harvests, the fortunes. A herald passes through your town every spring, and every spring the proclamation is a little longer.

choices.text: Learn what the proclamations really mean

effects.log: Read slowly, they say who is rising and who is falling at court.

choices.text: Make a friend of the herald

effects.log: The herald is lonely and talkative, and you hear court news before the court does.

events.text: War between the kingdoms. The roads fill with soldiers going one way and families going the other. In the square of your town, the recruiters set up a table under the old tree.

choices.text: Help the families on the road

effects.log: You carry, you feed, you point the way. Nobody writes it down.

choices.text: Watch the soldiers and learn

effects.log: You learn how armies move, and how much of war is walking.

events.text: The temples are full in this age. On the god's days the bells ring from every hill, and the priests are heard in the courts of kings. In the temple of your town, someone has painted the Maker on the wall, and the face is almost yours.

choices.text: Look at the painting a long time

effects.log: Something in you remembers being looked up at like that.

choices.text: Light a lamp before it

effects.log: You light a lamp to a god you once were. It is a strange feeling, and not a bad one.

events.text: Faith thins in this age. New prophets preach in the squares, temples close for want of oil, and people say the heaven of this world has gone quiet. Some of them are angry about it. More are only sad.

choices.text: Listen to a prophet

effects.log: The prophet is sincere and wrong, and very tired. You buy them a meal.

choices.text: Keep a temple lamp burning

effects.log: You keep one lamp lit in an empty temple through the whole winter. Someone notices.

events.text: A golden age: the harvests come in early, the roads are safe, and the scholars of three kingdoms write to each other about everything. In every market people are a little too sure it will last forever.

choices.text: Enjoy it while it lasts

effects.log: You enjoy it. Golden ages are for that.

choices.text: Write down what it is like

effects.log: You write it down plainly, for the people who will one day not believe it.

events.text: The first time the System shows you someone else's thread, you cannot stop seeing it. All day every face you pass has a faint line behind it, running off into the years, and the System hums as if it were proud of itself.

choices.text: Ask the System to show you less

effects.log: The lines fade to where you have to look for them. That is better.

choices.text: Look at your own reflection

effects.log: Your own thread is the only one it will not show you.

events.text: Knowing what is written for one person changes how you look at everyone. You watch a stranger buy bread and wonder whether their thread is short, or bright, or turning, and you have to sit down for a while.

choices.text: Remind yourself that most skies are ordinary

effects.log: It helps. Most skies are.

choices.text: Wonder what yours would say

effects.log: The System does not answer. You suspect that is an answer.

events.text: The thing the System showed you has come true, exactly as written. You knew it would. Knowing did not make it lighter; it only meant you saw it coming for longer.

choices.text: Ask the System whether it could have been different

effects.log: The System is silent a long time. Then: [Threads can be turned. They seldom are.] It says nothing more.

choices.text: Go and see them

effects.log: You go. Whatever the thread said, the person is still a person, and that turns out to matter.

events.text: There is a particular quiet that comes after a fate is fulfilled. The System keeps it with you for a day, as if it were mourning or celebrating, and could not decide which.

choices.text: Keep the quiet

effects.log: You keep it. At the end of the day the System says, very softly: [Noted.] Then nothing more.

choices.text: Fill it with work

effects.log: You work until the quiet goes. It does, eventually.

events.text: Turning a thread costs the System something you did not know it had. For a season its voice is thin and far away, and when it comes back it says only: [It held.] Somewhere, someone is walking an ordinary road and will never know why.

choices.text: Thank the System

effects.log: [Unnecessary,] it says. It sounds pleased.

choices.text: Promise not to do it often

effects.log: [Good,] it says, with real feeling.
